title: Just 80 Minutes Less Sleep Could Cause Weight Gain
paragraphs: Most people know that eating too much and exercising too little can lead to weight gain. However, a new study from the United States suggests that losing even a small amount of sleep every night could also make people put on weight.

The study was carried out by researchers at Columbia University, led by Marie-Pierre St-Onge, and it was published in the journal Annals of Internal Medicine in 2026. It involved 95 adults who normally slept seven to eight hours a night. Many of them had a higher risk of heart and metabolic disease.

Each participant took part in two six-week periods. In one period, they slept as usual. In the other, they went to bed 90 minutes later than usual. Their sleep and activity were tracked using devices worn on their wrists. On average, they slept about 80 minutes less each night during the shorter-sleep period.

The researchers found that when people slept less, they gained about one pound, or 0.45 kilograms, on average. They also spent more time sitting down, about 17 extra minutes a day. Among men and women who had gone through menopause, the increase was almost 30 minutes a day. This extra sitting time was not explained only by the participants being awake for longer.

According to Faris Zuraikat, the study's first author, one pound may not seem like a lot, but it was gained in just six weeks. Zuraikat believes that losing this amount of sleep for a whole year could lead to a significant weight gain. However, this is only an estimate.
Most earlier research on sleep and weight looked at people who slept only about four hours a night for short periods. St-Onge said that getting enough sleep may help reduce the risk of weight gain.
